Class TuiRunner

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tui.TuiRunner
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class TuiRunner extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Main entry point for running TUI applications.

TuiRunner handles the terminal lifecycle (raw mode, alternate screen, cursor), event parsing, and the main event loop. 

try (var tui = TuiRunner.create()) {
    tui.run(
        (event, runner) -> {
            if (event instanceof KeyEvent && ((KeyEvent) event).isQuit()) {
                runner.quit();
                return false;
            }
            return handleEvent(event);
        },
        frame -> renderUI(frame)
    );
}

    • run

      public void run(EventHandler handler, Renderer renderer) throws Exception
      Runs the main event loop with the given handler and renderer.

      Exceptions thrown during rendering are caught and handled according to the configured RenderErrorHandler. By default, errors are displayed in the UI and the application waits for user dismissal before quitting.

      Parameters:
      handler - the event handler
      renderer - the UI renderer
      Throws:
      Exception - if an error occurs during execution that cannot be handled

    • pollEvent

      public Event pollEvent(Duration timeout)
      Polls for the next event with the specified timeout.

      Events are read from the unified event queue, which receives events from both the dedicated input reader thread (keyboard/mouse) and the scheduler thread (ticks/resize).

      Input events (key/mouse) are prioritized over tick events to ensure UI responsiveness even when rendering is slow.

      Parameters:
      timeout - the maximum time to wait
      Returns:
      the next event, or null if timeout expires

    • runOnRenderThread

      public void runOnRenderThread(Runnable action)
      Executes an action on the render thread.

      If called from the render thread, the action is executed immediately. If called from another thread, the action is queued for execution on the render thread.

      This is the primary API for safely updating UI state from background threads: 

      // From a background thread:
runner.runOnRenderThread(() -> {
    updateState();
    // UI will redraw on next event
});
      Parameters:
      action - the action to execute on the render thread

    • runLater

      public void runLater(Runnable action)
      Queues an action to be executed on the render thread.

      Unlike runOnRenderThread(Runnable), this method always queues the action even if called from the render thread. This is useful when you want to defer execution until after the current event handling completes.

      Parameters:
      action - the action to execute on the render thread

    • dispatch

      public void dispatch(Event event)
      Dispatches an event into the event queue.

      Primarily for testing: allows tests to inject key, mouse, or resize events without going through the backend. The event is processed on the next iteration of the event loop. Has no effect if the runner is not running.

      Parameters:
      event - the event to dispatch

    • scheduler

      public ScheduledExecutorService scheduler()
      Returns the shared scheduler for scheduling tasks.

      This scheduler runs on a dedicated daemon thread. Tasks scheduled here execute on the scheduler thread, not the render thread. To modify UI state from a scheduled task, use runOnRenderThread(Runnable).

      Returns:
      the scheduler (never null)

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes this runner and releases resources.

      If a scheduler was provided via configuration, it is NOT shut down - the caller retains ownership and is responsible for its lifecycle. If no scheduler was provided, the internally-created scheduler is shut down.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable

    • builder

      public static TuiRunner.Builder builder()
      Returns a new builder for constructing TuiRunner instances.

      The builder provides a fluent API for configuring all aspects of the TUI application including bindings and auto-registration of action handlers. 

      TuiRunner.builder()
    .bindings(BindingSets.vim())
    .eventHandler(app)
    .renderer(app::render)
    .autoBindingRegistration(true)
    .build()
    .run();
      Returns:
      a new builder
